caption: Figure 7: An example of B-node operations. In this example, A and C are talking to each other, B talks to herself (idle client), and the message from someone to D is blocked.
subject: how B-nodes obliviously sort, detect/patch/swap, and re-sort message records to pair conversations and hide access patterns

groups.why_chosen: Sorting message records by private label makes same-label pairs adjacent so they can be detected, patched and swapped into complete sender/receiver pairs, then re-sorting by entry_id restores each enclave's original slots without ever revealing who talked to whom.
groups.what_to_learn: a grid of small record-tables repeated in successive columns to show a multi-pass sort/transform pipeline; colour- and value-linking a handful of tracked records across frames whose row/column position is not stable; numbered stage-name boxes placed between columns rather than inside them
